Rebuttal

/rih-BUT-ul/ - the stress falls on BUT · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Rebuttal means an argument made to counter or disprove a claim.

The debate coach grades every rebuttal on one question: did it answer the argument actually made, or the one you wish they'd made?

Worked Example

The star witness swore the warehouse stood empty by six. The defense's rebuttal needed no stack of exhibits — only the courthouse clock and the ferry timetable: if the warehouse emptied at six, the witness was still mid-river at the moment he claims he watched it happen.

A rebuttal answers a specific claim and sets out to take it apart with reasons or evidence. Direction separates it from a polemic, which attacks a standing position uninvited — a rebuttal is always a reply. And a bare 'that's false' is not yet a rebuttal; the form demands grounds.

How Rebuttal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

counterargument

counterargument: the case built against a claim

rejoinder

rejoinder: a sharp answering reply in an exchange

Antonyms

surrender

surrender: giving up the point instead of answering it

agreement

agreement: accepting the claim as true

How Strong Is It? — denial → rebuttal → refutation

denial vs. rebuttal

denial vs. rebuttal: A denial is weaker than a rebuttal — it rejects the claim flatly but brings no reasons to the table.

refutation vs. rebuttal

refutation vs. rebuttal: A refutation goes further than a rebuttal: a rebuttal argues against the claim, while a refutation finishes it, proving the thing false outright.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of rebuttal.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back (Latin)

Root — butt

Root — butt: to strike, push (Old French boter)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: noun: the act of

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) + butt (strike) + -al = a striking-back. Old French boter meant to shove or strike — the same blow as in a goat butting a gate — so a rebuttal is an argument shoved back at the one who advanced it.

Use the root in a new word: butt

Use the root in a new word: butt: Mountain goats butt heads all spring to settle who leads the herd.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / debate

Rebuttal belongs to structured argument — courtrooms, debate rounds, letters answering letters. A quick jab in conversation is a retort; proof that ends the matter is a refutation; and when the attack arrives uninvited rather than in reply, you are reading a polemic.
